item.title: Records Retrieval
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-07-06

Pursuant to Section 3-05 of the NYC Procurement Policy Board Rules, it is the intent of the Administration for Children's Services  (ACS) to enter into sole source negotiations with Iron Mountain Inc.  located at One Federal Street, Boston, MA 02110.

ACS expects that Iron Mountain, Inc., will be awarded a contract to provide current ACS case records currently stored in their warehouse by Sheltering Arms. 

Any vendor besides Iron Mountain that believes it can provide these services should contact Mr. Michael Walker at michael.walker2@acs.nyc.gov.  Responses are due by Noon, July 6, 2026.

item.title: Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children (CSEC)
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $694K | Vendor: The Children's Village

This Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children (CSEC) Renewal will continue year-round programming to assess for and prevent sex and labor trafficking for trafficked youth and youth at risk for trafficking. This program would include teaching and coaching youth on topics such as healthy relationships, safer sex practices and community safety, using developmentally appropriate engagement strategies; and would provide individual assessments, group workshops, and referrals to community-based organizations for youth and training for staff. The total contract amount is $693,750.00 ($555,000.00 + $138,750.00  25% allowance allocation).

item.title: Negotiated Acquisition Extension for Alternative to Placement and Aftercare Services
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $510K | Vendor: Jewish Board of Family and Children's Services Inc

Pursuant to the Procurement Policy Board Rules, Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii), the Administration for Children's Services seeks to utilize the Negotiated Acquisition Extension procurement method to extend its contract with the Jewish Board of Family and Children's Services for Alternative to Placement and Aftercare Services - Juvenile Justice Initiatives - Staten Island for 11/15/2026 to 6/30/27. The extension period -from November 15, 2026, to June 30, 2027-will provide ACS with sufficient time to finalize a new RFP with an anticipated release on or before July 31, 2026. The resulting award will begin on July 1, 2027. This extension will ensure continuity of services and support ACSs strategic alignment of all ATP contracts to the Citys fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027.

item.title: Childcare and Chaperone Services - Renewal #2
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $6.3M | Vendor: Gotham Per Diem Inc.

ACS's Office of Preplacement Services (OPS) works to provide a safe and nurturing environment for children and youth entering and/or reentering the foster care system. The Nicholas Scoppetta Children's Center (Children's Center) is a multi-departmental setting that houses children and youth awaiting foster care placements, is the first step in permanency planning for children entering and re-entering the foster care system. ACS is seeking a qualified contractor to provide Childcare and Chaperone Services to children and youth, including to children with special needs, i.e., children who are classified as developmentally delayed, with medical conditions/medically fragile, autistic and/or children having a mental health diagnosis.

item.title: Translation Services
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $984K | Vendor: Language Line Services, Inc.

The Immigrant Services and Language Affairs (ISLA) division of The NYC Administration for Childrens Services (ACS) is seeking three vendors to provide In-Person/VRI interpretation for Spoken Languages, Deaf/Hard-of-Hearing Interpretation and Language services, and Written Translation Services. This procurement will assist ACS compliance with Local Law 73 (2003), Local Law 30 (2017), the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II, and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which require ACS and its network of providers to provide interpretation and translation services for all limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families to enable equal access to ACS services, as well as ensure best practice for casework with limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families. The term of each of the contracts will be July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2029.

item.title: Alternative to Detention Renewal #1
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $4.0M | Vendor: Justice Innovation Inc

To provide pre-dispositional supervision and services to court-involved youth as an alternative to detention (ATD). ATD is a part of a larger graduated continuum of citywide services targeting Family Court-involved juveniles. ACSs goals and objectives for this RFP are to provide a continuum of effective ATD programming across the City for youth 12 to 18 years old who, absent these programs, would likely be placed in an ACS detention facility.
